label: History
value: The Cowardly Lion met Dorothy Gale in a forest along the Yellow Brick Road.
unit: The Cowardly Lion first met Dorothy Gale, Toto, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman in a forest along the Yellow Brick Road when he tried to attack Toto, prompting Dorothy to slap his nose. Ashamed of his cowardice, he joined Dorothy's quest to Emerald City in hopes that the Wizard of Oz would grant him courage. During the journey, he repeatedly risked his life to save his companions by leaping across dangerous chasms, carrying them across a river, and holding off wild Kalidahs. Upon reaching the Emerald City, the Wizard promised to grant his request if the party destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West. In the Winkie Country, the Lion was captured and caged by the Witch after refusing to be harnessed like a horse, but Dorothy secretly fed him until the Witch was melted. After returning to the Emerald City, the Wizard gave him a potion from a square green bottle, telling him it was courage, which immediately boosted his confidence. On their subsequent journey to the South, the Lion defeated a monstrous Giant Spider threatening an ancient forest, earning the gratitude of the beasts who declared him their King. Afterwards, he rejoined his friends to visit Glinda and eventually said a tearful goodbye to Dorothy before returning to rule his forest domain.

label: History
value: Dorothy lived on a small farm in Kansas
unit: Dorothy lived on a small farm in Kansas with her Aunt Em, Uncle Henry, and her dog Toto until a powerful cyclone swept their farmhouse away into the magical Land of Oz. Upon landing, her house accidentally crushed the Wicked Witch of the East, earning her the gratitude of the Munchkins and the witch's Silver Shoes. Advised by the Good Witch of the North, Dorothy set out along the Yellow Brick Road toward the Emerald City to seek the aid of the Great Wizard of Oz. Along the way, she befriended and recruited the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion. The Wizard agreed to help her only if she destroyed the Wicked Witch of the West, which Dorothy eventually accomplished by throwing a bucket of water over the witch when she attempted to steal one of Dorothy's Silver Shoes. After discovering the Wizard was a fraud who accidentally departed in a balloon without her, Dorothy journeyed to the South to seek Glinda the Good Witch. Glinda revealed that the magical Silver Shoes had possessed the power to carry her anywhere all along, allowing Dorothy to click her heels three times and safely return home to Kansas.

label: History
value: Dorothy Gale and her companions travel to the South seeking a way back to Kansas.
unit: When Dorothy Gale and her companions travel to the South seeking a way back to Kansas, Glinda receives them in her palace. She reveals to Dorothy that the Silver Shoes she wore all along had the power to carry her home. After receiving the Golden Cap from Dorothy, Glinda uses its three wishes to return the Scarecrow to the Emerald City, the Tin Woodman to the Winkie Country, and the Cowardly Lion to the ancient forest before releasing the Winged Monkeys forever. Later, when Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman seek her aid against General Jinjur's usurping army, Glinda consults her Great Book of Records and reveals that Ozma, the rightful princess of Oz, was hidden away by Mombi. Glinda marches on the Emerald City, forces the wicked witch Mombi to undo the enchantment on the enchantment-bound boy Tip, and restores Princess Ozma to her rightful throne.

label: History
value: Jack Pumpkinhead was carved out of a pumpkin.
unit: Jack Pumpkinhead was carved and built out of branches and a pumpkin by a boy named Tip in the Gillikin Country to frighten the witch Mombi. Instead of being frightened, Mombi used her newly acquired Powder of Life to bring Jack to life as a test. Tip later fled from Mombi's home and brought Jack along, with Jack regarding Tip as his father. Together with the Sawhorse, which was also brought to life by the Powder of Life, they traveled to the Emerald City. Upon arriving, Jack met the Scarecrow, the ruler of Oz, and the two formed a fast friendship due to their shared non-human natures. When General Jinjur's Army of Revolt besieged the Emerald City, Jack accompanied Tip, the Scarecrow, and their companions on a series of escapes and adventures across Oz, culminating in the restoration of Princess Ozma to the throne.

label: History
value: General Jinjur raises an Army of Revolt.
unit: General Jinjur raises an Army of Revolt composed entirely of young women armed with knitting needles. Capitalizing on the Scarecrow's absence, she marches on the Emerald City and successfully captures it, forcing the male populace to do housework while the women take control. She crowns herself ruler and spends her days lounging in the palace eating caramels and wearing the city's jewels. When the Scarecrow returns with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Sawhorse, Jinjur manages to keep them at bay initially using her army and the help of Mombi. However, when Glinda the Good Arrives with her army and Glinda's allies release fierce animals into the palace, Jinjur and her soldiers panic. label: History
value: Mombi lived in the Gillikin Country
unit: Mombi lived in the Gillikin Country with a boy named Tip, whom she treated as a servant. When Tip attempted to scare her with a pumpkin-headed wooden man named Jack, Mombi instead used the Powder of Life to bring Jack to life, intending to turn Tip into a marble statue as punishment. Tip fled with Jack, prompting Mombi to ally herself with General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt to conquer the Emerald City. During the siege and subsequent takeover, Mombi used her magic to help Jinjur retain control and thwart the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and their allies. Eventually, Glinda the Good Witch intervened and captured Mombi, forcing her to reveal the secret of Princess Ozma's fate. Mombi confessed that she had transformed the young princess into Tip years ago, and Glinda compelled her to perform the enchantment that restored Tip to Princess Ozma, stripping Mombi of her magical powers as punishment.

label: History
value: Ozma was born as the royal princess of Oz.
unit: Ozma was born as the royal princess of Oz, the daughter of King Pastoria. When the Wizard of Oz took power, he entrusted the infant princess to the old witch Mombi, who transformed her into a boy named Tip to keep her true heritage hidden. Growing up under Mombi's harsh care in the Gillikin Country, Tip had no memory of his former life. Seeking to frighten Mombi, Tip constructed Jack Pumpkinhead and brought him to life using Mombi's Powder of Life. After running away from Mombi, Tip journeyed to the Emerald City, where he helped Jack, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Woggle-Bug, and the Gump escape General Jinjur's rebel army. With the aid of Glinda the Good Witch, Jinjur was defeated, and Glinda forced Mombi to confess her secrets. Mombi restored Tip to her original form as Princess Ozma, who then took her rightful throne as the monarch of the Land of Oz.

Growing up under Mombi's harsh care in the Gillikin Country, Tip had no memory of his former life. Seeking to frighten Mombi, Tip constructed Jack Pumpkinhead and brought him to life using Mombi's Powder of Life. After running away from Mombi, Tip journeyed to the Emerald City, where he helped Jack, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Woggle-Bug, and the Gump escape General Jinjur's rebel army. With the aid of Glinda the Good Witch, Jinjur was defeated, and Glinda forced Mombi to confess her secrets. Mombi restored Tip to her original form as Princess Ozma, who then took her rightful throne as the monarch of the Land of Oz.

value: Pastoria was the rightful king of the Land of Oz.
unit: Pastoria was the rightful king of the Land of Oz, belonging to the long-standing royal house that governed from the Emerald City. When the Wizard arrived in Oz in a hot air balloon, the local populace believed the stranger to be a great sorcerer and granted him the throne, leading to Pastoria's removal from power. Before or during these events, Pastoria's infant daughter, Princess Ozma, was secretly handed over to the witch Mombi to hide her true identity and royal heritage. By the end of The Marvelous Land of Oz, Pastoria's history is brought to light as Mombi reveals how she enchanted Ozma into the boy Tip, ultimately restoring Pastoria's royal heir to the throne.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse was carved by Tip.
unit: The Saw-Horse was carved by Tip using a carpenter's bench and brought to life when Tip sprinkled it with the magic Powder of Life to test the spell's effectiveness. After coming to life, the Saw-Horse lacked a mouth until Tip carved one for it, enabling it to talk and hold reins. It served as a fast mount for Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead on their journey to the Emerald City. Along the way, it damaged one of its legs in an accident, which was subsequently repaired by the Tin Woodman using gold plating. The Saw-Horse carried the party through various perils during the revolt against General Jinjur and proved instrumental in helping the travelers escape to Winkie Country and seek aid from Glinda the Good. Ultimately, it assisted in restoring Princess Ozma to the throne of Oz.

After coming to life, the Saw-Horse lacked a mouth until Tip carved one for it, enabling it to talk and hold reins. It served as a fast mount for Tip and Jack Pumpkinhead on their journey to the Emerald City. Along the way, it damaged one of its legs in an accident, which was subsequently repaired by the Tin Woodman using gold plating. The Saw-Horse carried the party through various perils during the revolt against General Jinjur and proved instrumental in helping the travelers escape to Winkie Country and seek aid from Glinda the Good. Ultimately, it assisted in restoring Princess Ozma to the throne of Oz.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow met Dorothy in a Munchkin cornfield.
unit: After meeting Dorothy in a Munchkin cornfield, the Scarecrow decided to accompany her to the Emerald City to ask the Wonderful Wizard of Oz for brains. Along the yellow brick road, he proved his natural intelligence repeatedly by devising plans to rescue his friends from the Kalidahs, cross deep chasms, and escape a poppy field. Upon reaching the Wizard, he was tasked with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West, which the group accomplished. The Wizard later presented him with 'brains' made of sawdust, pins, and needles, giving him immense confidence. Before leaving in a balloon, the Wizard appointed the Scarecrow as the new ruler of the Emerald City. In Volume 2, General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt besieged the Emerald City, forcing the Scarecrow to flee and seek help from the Tin Woodman. Together with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, and the Woggle-Bug, they eventually enlisted the aid of Glinda the Good to liberate the city and restore the rightful heir, Princess Ozma, to the throne.

label: Personality
value: The Tin Woodman is extremely tender-hearted.

Because he believes he lacks a natural heart, he strives extra hard to be kind and loving. He is deeply loyal to his friends and willing to face danger to protect them. However, he is prone to weeping when moved or saddened, which causes his tin jaws to rust shut if he is not careful.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman was rusted in the forest for a year.
unit: After being rusted in the forest for a year, the Tin Woodman was discovered and oiled by Dorothy Gale and the Scarecrow. He joined Dorothy on her journey along the yellow brick road to the Emerald City, hoping the Wizard of Oz would give him a heart. Along the way, he used his axe to assist the group, chopping down trees and defending them from threats. Upon reaching Oz, the Wizard tasked the companions with defeating the Wicked Witch of the West; during their quest, the Tin Woodman was dropped onto sharp rocks by the Winged Monkeys and battered into tin junk. After Dorothy defeated the Witch, the Winkies repaired the Tin Woodman and invited him to become their ruler, which he accepted after completing his quest. Returning to the Emerald City, he received a velvet-and-sawdust heart from the Wizard. He then helped Dorothy journey to the South to see Glinda. Later, when General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt overthrew the Scarecrow in the Emerald City, the Scarecrow escaped to the West to seek the Tin Woodman's aid. Reunited, they set out to reclaim the throne, eventually forming a party with Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, and the Woggle-Bug, and defeating the rebels with the aid of Glinda.

label: History
value: Tip grows up in the Gillikin Country.
unit: Tip grows up in the Gillikin Country under the harsh care of the witch Mombi. To frighten Mombi, Tip constructs a man made of pumpkin and wood, naming him Jack Pumpkinhead. Mombi uses the Powder of Life to bring Jack to life, and after Tip learns she intends to turn him into a marble statue, he runs away with Jack. Along their journey, Tip uses the Powder of Life to animate the Sawhorse, which becomes their mount. Arriving at the Emerald City, they find it besieged by General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt. Tip joins forces with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and later the Woggle-Bug to reclaim the throne. After building the Gump to escape Jinjur's forces, the companions seek the aid of Glinda the Good Sorceress. Glinda discovers that Tip is actually Princess Ozma, the rightful ruler of Oz who was transformed into a boy by Mombi. Glinda forces Mombi to reverse the spell, restoring Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma, who then takes her rightful place on the throne of Oz.

label: History
value: Toto lived in Kansas with Dorothy and her family.
unit: Toto lived in Kansas with Dorothy and her family, serving as her constant companion and making her laugh in the gray prairie environment. When a cyclone struck Kansas, Toto hid under the bed, causing Dorothy to linger in the house to catch him, which resulted in them both being carried away inside the house to the Land of Oz. Throughout their journey along the Yellow Brick Road, Toto accompanied Dorothy, making friends with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion. He famously tipped over the screen in the Emerald City throne room, revealing that the Wizard was merely an ordinary man from Omaha. After traveling to the South to see Glinda the Good Witch, Toto returned home safely to Kansas with Dorothy when she clicked her Silver Shoes together.

When a cyclone struck Kansas, Toto hid under the bed, causing Dorothy to linger in the house to catch him, which resulted in them both being carried away inside the house to the Land of Oz. Throughout their journey along the Yellow Brick Road, Toto accompanied Dorothy, making friends with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion. He famously tipped over the screen in the Emerald City throne room, revealing that the Wizard was merely an ordinary man from Omaha. After traveling to the South to see Glinda the Good Witch, Toto returned home safely to Kansas with Dorothy when she clicked her Silver Shoes together.

value: The Wizard relies on deception

He acts out of self-preservation and fear of being exposed by the wicked witches.

label: History
value: Oscar Diggs is a circus ventriloquist
unit: Oscar Diggs, a circus ventriloquist and balloonist from Omaha, drifted in a hot-air balloon to the Land of Oz. The local inhabitants believed he was a powerful wizard who fell from the sky, so he assumed rule over the realm. To secure his power, he hid the rightful heir, the baby Princess Ozma, by entrusting her to the witch Mombi. He then ordered the building of the Emerald City, making everyone wear green spectacles to make the city appear made entirely of emeralds. Fearing the genuine magical powers of the Wicked Witches of the East and West, he isolated himself in his palace and used props and illusions to maintain his fearful reputation. When Dorothy Gale and her companions arrived seeking favors, he demanded they slay the Wicked Witch of the West before he would grant their wishes. After Dorothy succeeded, Toto accidentally knocked over a screen in the throne room, revealing the Wizard as a fraud. Despite his trickery, he fulfilled his promises by giving the Scarecrow brains, the Tin Woodman a heart, and the Cowardly Lion courage through symbolic means. He constructed a hot-air balloon to take Dorothy and himself back to Kansas, but the balloon prematurely launched with only him aboard, leaving his current fate and destination unknown.

label: History
value: The Woggle-Bug originally was a small, ordinary bug.
unit: Originally a small, ordinary bug residing under the hearthstone of a country schoolhouse, the Woggle-Bug absorbed years of lessons taught by the schoolmaster to his pupils. One day, he was captured by the schoolmaster, who displayed him under a magic lantern to demonstrate insect anatomy to the class. Highly magnified upon the screen, the bug managed to step off the projection and escape into the outside world while maintaining his large size. Adding the titles 'Highly Magnified' and 'Thoroughly Educated' to his name, he dressed in fine clothes and set off to tour Oz. Along his travels, he meets Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Sawhorse, and the Scarecrow as they flee from General Jinjur's Army of Revolt. Joining their party, he offers his intellectual wisdom and frequent puns as they journey to consult Glinda the Good. He remains a steadfast companion through their battles using the Gump, and he attends the assembly where Princess Ozma is restored to the throne of Oz.
